activities.anchor: the drawing's itinerary and its handwriting at once
activities.caption: match each line division to its job
activities.name: lsvLineMatch

config.prompt: Line's working divisions — match each to its job:

pairs.right: describes an edge — slow, deliberate, the boundary where one thing ends
the 30-second skeleton capture — the curve of weight and action, drawn too fast for the analytical mind to interrupt
lines promoted to tone — parallel strokes whose density builds value, direction building form
a confident continuous stroke reads as certainty; a searching, broken line as observation in progress

config.why: Dürer's engravings are hatching's permanent exhibition, and Ingres versus Delacroix is the quality shorthand — cool analytic line against baroque energy. The eye reads the stroke before it reads the subject.

activities.anchor: shapes with outlines and proportions like any others
activities.caption: positive or negative shape?
activities.name: lsvSpaceSort

config.prompt: Beginners draw objects; the trained eye draws both — file each shape:

items.label: the sliver of background inside an elbow

config.why: A negative space has no symbol, so the brain must actually look — draw the chair only as its surrounding and interstitial voids and the positive shape materialises, usually more accurate than any direct attempt.

activities.anchor: build the scale with your medium first
activities.caption: the five-step value scale, light to dark
activities.name: lsvScaleOrder

config.prompt: A readable image needs five values, not twenty — assemble the scale:
config.why: The squint test blurs colour and detail away and leaves the value pattern — what the viewer's eye reads from across the room. Detail rides on the value structure; it cannot replace one.

activities.caption: name the sphere's two problem tones
activities.name: lsvSphereCloze

config.text: On a single sphere under one light: the %%0%% marks where the surface turns away from the light — the value step-off point — and %%1%% on the lower rim is light bounced from the table: present, but never as bright as the directly lit side.
config.hint: One is the step-off point; one is borrowed from the table.

activities.caption: one line of this finishing plan is wrong
activities.name: lsvEdgeSpot

config.prompt: One line of this finishing plan is wrong — click it:
lines: Impasto, collage and paper grain are actual texture — physically present.
Implied texture: a few accurate marks of roughness read as a whole rough surface.
Render every centimetre of the surface so nothing is left ambiguous.
Hard edges shout and collect the eye; soft edges whisper and recede.
Vermeer loses his backgrounds' edges so the pearl's highlight can win.
config.correction: Rendering every centimetre kills the image's hierarchy — implied texture is best rationed, and sharpness is spent only where attention is wanted; the rest goes soft or lost.
config.why: Sargent keeps a handful of razor edges and loses the rest — the viewer experiences the management as depth, light and focus.

activities.anchor: the cheapest quality-control instrument ever invented
activities.caption: fifteen minutes a day vs the monthly marathon
activities.name: lsvPracCompare

config.prompt: Two practice schedules, same weekly hours — drag the divider:

before.label: fifteen minutes a day
before.text: frequent short reps with immediate feedback — gesture at 30 seconds, blind contour at ten minutes, squint-and-compare as you go; skill acquisition research is unambiguous

after.label: the monthly four-hour session
after.text: occasional heroics — the same hours arrive too late to compound, and the feedback loop is a month long

config.why: Materials stay neutral — pencil, ink, charcoal, pixel: each medium's friction just teaches a different discipline on the same grammar.

activities.caption: the picture shouts in three directions — fix it
activities.name: lsvFocalBranch

config.root: A portfolio review flags your still life: 'it shouts in three directions and is heard in none.' The arrangement grammar has fixes — which do you run?

choices.label: Demote to accents — keep one primary focal point, at most two subordinate
choices.feedback: Weight, contrast and edges conspire at the focal point — hierarchy restored.

choices.label: Give all three equal weight and let the viewer choose
choices.feedback: The eye settles at the centre of weight whether the designer chose it or not — composition is making that landing spot intentional.

choices.label: Move each focal point onto a rule-of-thirds intersection
choices.feedback: Training wheels: the grid is a default, not a fix — the entry, the path and the rest still need scripting.

hierarchy.text: One primary and at most two subordinate accents — the picture is heard in one direction.

democracy.text: Equal weight is still a decision — an unintentional one, and the loudest contrast wins by accident.

grid.text: Placement helps, but a strong composition scripts the journey: a light corridor leading in, a diagonal for movement, the sharpest edge at the destination.

config.why: Balance comes in kinds — symmetrical, asymmetrical, radial — and the frame's own edges count: an object touching an edge drags the eye outward.

activities.caption: true or false — what 'good drawing' means
activities.name: lsvGoodJudge

statements.s: 'Good drawing' means contour accuracy, so practice means more outline copying.
statements.why: The compositional work — value structure, shape interlock, edge hierarchy — happens on a different layer than outline.

statements.s: Many weak drawings are contour-accurate and compositionally dead.
statements.why: Accuracy on one layer cannot substitute for the others — practise them separately: notan for structure, gesture for movement, blind contour for observation.

statements.s: The elements have not changed in five centuries; the settings have.
statements.why: Mastery is configuration, not invention — every era re-weighted the same four elements.
